annotations.text: The one view. Four priorities, starred at three different levels — a goal, a plan inside a goal, a task inside a goal. Each card is the Goal for context; the star sits where you put it. Health is a lane at rest: it still exists, it just isn't asking for anything.

Same view, 13 priorities. The app never warns you. It simply can't give 13 things room, so the tasks fall out of the cards, Work wraps onto a second row, and the page stops fitting on one screen. Overload is something you SEE, not something you're told.
"I have fifteen minutes." The size lens is a filter on the same view, not a mode — nothing moves, the tasks that don't fit just fall away. This is what replaced the separate Picker screen.
The other half of the toggle. Unprioritised goals come back as quiet outlined cards — present, legible, not competing. Going looking for work is one click, not a different place.

Set new priorities — UC-3030, and the only sanctioned nudge in the app. "Coming up" shows what has a deadline, how far out it is, and what's left; you can star straight from it. Nowhere else does the app raise a date on its own.

Goal detail — UC-2030, UC-2040, UC-5010, UC-1060. SUPERSEDED at M4: drilling in became opening a card in place, and a second surface would be the mode the view exists to avoid. Kept as the record of that decision; PRD §12 says so too.
Quick capture — UC-1010, UC-1030. One line, destination optional, defaults to The Pile.
Break it down — UC-2050, and all three outs of UC-4050 in the footer.
The Pile — UC-1040, UC-1050, UC-1070. Reachable from the top bar, with no count anywhere to pull at you.

One rule for all four cases: the card is always the Goal, the star renders where you actually put it, and everything you did not star folds into a faint line. A tighter commitment takes less room on screen — which is what keeps the view honest when you star a dozen things.

How things are made and how they change level — UC-2011, 2012, 2025, 2026, 2057, 2059. The ladder is one mechanism, not four: a task that turns out to be an outcome climbs, a goal that turns out to be a step descends, and everything it carries comes with it.

The four exits, and the two dialogs that matter — UC-2105, 2106, 2130, 2131, 2132. Delete always shows Archive beside it, reading first. In the Archive, two of those goals were finished and two were abandoned, and nothing on screen tells you which.
